data.long_meaning: Mah- We (great) + Wesh (power). The name Mahwesh carries the meaning “Great Power” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Parents who choose Mahwesh usually hope their child will grow to embody great power and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mahwesh, derived from the Sanskrit language used in Hinduism, implies great power. In Hindu culture, power is often attributed to various gods and goddesses, and the belief in the power of names is deeply rooted. Naming a child with a powerful name is seen as a way to ensure that the child will be blessed with courage, strength, and the ability to overcome challenges in life.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the belief is that every name has a spiritual energy, or vibration, associated with it. The name Mahwesh, with its roots in the Sanskrit language, is believed to carry the spiritual energy of great power. This energy is thought to protect and guide the individual bearing the name, helping them to overcome obstacles and fulfill their dharma. The name Mahwesh can serve as a constant reminder of the inner strength and power each individual possesses, helping them to tap into this power during times of challenge or adversity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mahwesh: Goddess of Auspicious Beginnings and Prosperity. Her name signifies the blessing of abundant joy and success in all new endeavors.

historical_references.reference: Mahawesh was a Hindu warrior from the Saurashtra region in Gujarat, India. He was a general in the army of the Chalukya king, Jayasimha Siddharaja I (r. 1143-1157 CE). Mahawesh played a significant role in the Chalukya victories against the Solanki and the Chahamanas.

Another reference to Mahawesh is found in the writings of the Jain scholar Hemachandra, who lived during the 12th and 13th centuries CE. In his works, Hemachandra mentions Mahawesh as a Jain patron and a donor to Jain temples in the Saurashtra region.
